bull.b: Exceptional revenue growth shows rapidly increasing demand for Nebius’s AI cloud infrastructure and expanding customer adoption. If sustained, this scale can improve infrastructure utilization, strengthen market position, and provide a durable base for compounding revenue over the next several quarters.

A large contracted backlog improves medium-term revenue visibility, while substantial upfront customer payments help fund infrastructure expansion before all capacity is operational. Together, these commitments can support planning, liquidity, and customer retention as Nebius scales its platform.

The move from negative to strongly positive adjusted EBITDA indicates operating leverage as the core AI business scales. Sustained margins at this level would improve internal funding capacity, support reinvestment in infrastructure, and demonstrate stronger economics for the company’s principal growth engine.

bear.b: The required investment in GPUs, data centers, and related infrastructure creates substantial execution and funding demands. Large recurring capital outlays can pressure free cash flow and raise the consequences of construction delays, slower customer onboarding, or capacity arriving before revenue.

bear.t: Operating Losses and Weak Cash Conversion
bear.b: Despite strong growth and improved adjusted results, persistent core operating losses indicate that the business has not yet established consistent profitability on a reported basis. Deeply negative free cash flow further limits self-funding capacity and increases dependence on successful scaling and financing.

The step-up in leverage reduces financial flexibility while Nebius is pursuing an exceptionally large infrastructure build-out. Continued reliance on debt and equity issuance can increase financing costs, expose the company to capital-market conditions, and create dilution risk for existing shareholders.
